title: Chapter Map: Local Forms To Global Obstructions
notes: Open the lecture by naming the organizing problem rather than listing topics. The chapter asks how local differential-form data can be assembled into a global invariant. Good covers make local pieces simple, double complexes record how they meet, and sphere bundles show what obstruction remains when assembly cannot be completed.

title: The Cech-de Rham Double Complex
notes: Use this slide to fix the coordinate system for the whole lecture. Horizontal motion is the Cech coboundary across intersections, while vertical motion is the exterior derivative inside each open set. The sign in the total differential is the first place students should see that bookkeeping is doing mathematical work.

title: Good Covers Make Columns Exact
notes: Emphasize why good covers are more than a pleasant hypothesis. If every finite intersection is contractible or empty, the Poincare lemma kills local higher cohomology. The hard-looking sheaf of forms then contributes exact columns, so the remaining information is forced into the combinatorics of overlaps.

title: Two Exits From One Total Complex
notes: Present the comparison theorem as two routes out of the same board. Exact Cech rows push a total cocycle toward global forms, recovering de Rham cohomology. Exact good-cover columns push the same information toward the bottom Cech row, recovering cohomology of the nerve with constant coefficients.

title: Cech Cohomology Becomes Nerve Cohomology
notes: The finite examples keep the abstract comparison honest. A three-set circle cover has a triangular nerve without its face, so one one-dimensional cycle survives. A sphere good cover can be modeled by the boundary of a tetrahedron, where the surviving class is two-dimensional instead of one-dimensional.

title: Collating Turns Cech Data Into A Form
notes: Now move from comparison to construction. A partition of unity supplies an operator that lowers Cech degree. Repeating that move converts a Cech cocycle into an ordinary closed form. For the circle, the discrete one-cocycle becomes a global one-form whose period detects the same generator.

title: Presheaves And Monodromy
notes: This slide should prevent the common shortcut that locally constant means globally constant. A locally constant presheaf has isomorphic local fibers, but a loop in the nerve may return by a nontrivial automorphism. The cohomology on a circle is controlled by fixed vectors and cokernels of the monodromy minus identity.

title: Sphere Bundles Start With Orientation
notes: Introduce sphere bundles as the same double-complex machine with a new geometric input. Local top cohomology classes of fibers must agree on overlaps before one can even ask for a global angular class. Orientability is the compatibility condition that lets the tic-tac-toe descent begin.

title: Euler Class As The Last Unclosed Edge
notes: Frame the Euler class as an obstruction, not just a named invariant. The attempted diagonal extension of local fiber-volume data nearly closes the board. The last horizontal Cech term that refuses to vanish is a cocycle on the base, and its de Rham image is the Euler class.

title: Local Degree Measures The Obstruction
notes: Use the unit tangent bundle of the sphere as the concrete measuring device. A vector field with an isolated singularity has a boundary map into the fiber circle. In the notebook model that boundary map winds twice, so the Euler number is two, matching the Euler characteristic of the sphere.

title: Thom Isomorphism Uses Compact Vertical Support
notes: The Thom portion repeats the double-complex idea after changing the coefficients of the vertical direction. Compact support in each fiber concentrates the vertical cohomology in the rank of the bundle. Once orientation makes those local generators compatible, the total complex collapses to a degree-shifted copy of the base.

title: Poincare Duality As A Pullback Story
notes: Connect the compact-support construction to intersections. A Thom form lives near the zero section and represents the class dual to that section. Pulling it back by the zero section gives the Euler class, while pulling it against a transverse section records the zero locus as a Poincare dual cycle.

title: The Tic-Tac-Toe Argument Template
notes: Summarize the proof method in operational language. Start with a cocycle in one corner, use exactness to solve one edge at a time, alternate directions with the total-complex sign convention, and watch where the process terminates. In easy cases it proves an isomorphism; in sphere-bundle cases it exposes an obstruction.

title: Chapter Takeaways And Next Bridge
notes: Close by connecting this chapter to the larger course. Chapter 2 teaches that double complexes turn local-to-global questions into controlled algebra. The same discipline prepares students for spectral sequences next, where the tic-tac-toe board is no longer solved in one pass but filtered page by page.
